0|b023e67512accd01d6daadb0244b3b430f3b2b6e|torvalds~linux|/home/usuario01/Titan-Files-Research/src/_00/output/C/torvalds~linux|False|"btrfs: avoid blocking on page locks with nowait dio on compressed range
If we are doing NOWAIT direct IO read/write and our inode has compressed
extents
column2: we call filemap_fdatawrite_range() against the range in order

column1: to wait for compressed writeback to complete
iomap_dio_rw() calls filemap_write_and_wait_range() once
enough to wait for compressed writeback to complete.
This call to filemap_fdatawrite_range() can block on page locks
the first writepages() on a range that we will try to compress results
only in queuing a work to compress the data while holding the pages
locked.
Even though the generic code at iomap_dio_rw() will do the right thing
and return -EAGAIN for NOWAIT requests in case there are pages in the
range
column2: we can still end up at btrfs_dio_iomap_begin() with pages in the

column1: range because either of the following can happen:
1) Memory mapped writes
column2: as we haven't locked the range yet;

column1: 2) Buffered reads might have started
the filemap_fdatawrite_range() call before locking the file range.
So don't call filemap_fdatawrite_range() at btrfs_dio_iomap_begin() if we
are doing a NOWAIT read/write. Instead call filemap_range_needs_writeback()
to check if there are any locked
return -EAGAIN if that's the case.
